_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 2.2. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: COLE sends a message to a stranger offering to sell him cocaine. COLE has no cocaine and never intended to get any. Which is correct?
options: He commits an offence of offering to supply a controlled drug
No offence, because he had no drugs
He commits possession with intent to supply
explanations: Incorrect: the offer is complete when made.
An offer to supply is also committed.

questions.scenario: BELL offers to supply 'ecstasy' to an undercover officer and hands over tablets that turn out to contain no controlled drug. Which is correct?
options: No offence because the tablets were fake
The offer to supply a controlled drug is still committed
explanations: Correct: the offence is the offer.
No possession of a controlled drug.
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 2.2 · Offer to supply – fake drugs

questions.scenario: At a party, AMY passes a cannabis joint she bought to her friend, who smokes some and passes it back. No money changes hands. Which is correct?
options: There can be no supply without payment
Passing the joint to her friend can amount to supply
Only the friend commits an offence

questions.scenario: DEAN agrees to drive a dealer to deliveries and acts as a lookout, but never touches the drugs. Which offence is most appropriate?
options: Being concerned in the supply of a controlled drug by another (s. 4(3)(b))

questions.scenario: To prove possession of a controlled drug, what must the prosecution generally show about the defendant's knowledge?
options: That he knew the exact drug
That he knew he had the thing (e.g. the package), subject to the s. 28 defence
That he intended to use it

questions.scenario: A forensic test finds only microscopic traces of cocaine on a banknote, not visible or measurable. Is possession likely proved?
options: No – the quantity must be enough to amount to something (visible, tangible, measurable)
Yes, if the note was in his wallet

questions.scenario: Which of the following is evidence often used to show possession with intent to supply?
options: A single small amount for personal use
Scales, deal bags, large amounts of cash and messages arranging sales

questions.scenario: A landlord knows his tenants regularly inject heroin in his flat. He does nothing. Has he committed an offence under s. 8 MDA 1971?
options: Yes, s. 8 covers all drug use on premises
No – s. 8 covers smoking cannabis/opium, production and supply, not injecting heroin
Yes, as long as he is the owner
Only if he supplied the needles

questions.scenario: The same landlord knows his tenants are selling cocaine from the flat and lets it continue. Which is correct?
options: He may commit an offence under s. 8(b) – knowingly permitting supply on premises

questions.scenario: Which activity is covered by s. 8(d) MDA 1971?
options: Smoking cannabis, cannabis resin or prepared opium

questions.scenario: A university student allows friends to smoke cannabis in his hall of residence room. Can he be an 'occupier'?
options: Yes, a person with sufficient control of the premises can be an occupier
Only if he pays rent monthly

questions.scenario: A mother finds cannabis in her son's bedroom and immediately flushes it down the toilet to stop him using it. Which defence may apply to possession?
options: s. 5(4)(a) – taking possession to prevent another committing an offence and destroying it as soon as possible

questions.scenario: A man finds a bag of tablets in the street and keeps them for a week 'meaning to hand them in'. Is the s. 5(4)(b) defence likely to succeed?
options: Yes, any intention to hand in is enough
Yes, if they were Class C
Unlikely – he must take all reasonable steps to deliver them into lawful custody as soon as possible
Yes, if he is of good character

questions.scenario: A defendant says he believed the powder was cocaine, but it was heroin. Can he rely on s. 28 MDA?
options: No – believing it was a different controlled drug is no defence
Only if he is a first-time offender

questions.scenario: Which of the following best describes the s. 28 defence about the substance?
options: He didn't intend to use it
He neither knew nor suspected nor had reason to suspect it was a controlled drug

questions.scenario: Under s. 23(2) MDA 1971, what threshold allows a constable to search a person for drugs?
options: Reasonable grounds to suspect the person is in possession of a controlled drug

questions.scenario: Who can issue a search warrant for premises under s. 23(3) MDA 1971?
A man pushes an officer away to stop her searching him under s. 23. Which offence (among others) may apply?
FRANK grows cannabis plants under lamps in his loft. Which offence is most specific?
Converting cocaine powder into crack cocaine is an example of…
A man leaves a bag of drugs with a friend; later the friend returns the bag to him. Can returning it amount to supply?
options: No, returning property is never supply

questions.scenario: Which class is cannabis under the MDA 1971 (⚠ check edition)?
Which class is heroin?
Amphetamine prepared for injection is…
Possession of a controlled drug includes having it in the custody of another person when…
Which law deals with 'legal highs' that are not controlled drugs?
Someone takes orders by phone for a dealer, but never handles drugs or money. Which is correct?
options: He may be concerned in the supply or in the making of an offer to supply by another

questions.scenario: Under s. 8, the occupier must ___ permit or suffer the activity.
